document_title: The Permit Knows Where the Machine Is
post_copy:
Two numbers and one blank sit in the stock table of the Arctic permit NMFS issued the Navy on September 10th.

Beaufort beluga. Abundance estimate 39,258 from a 1992 survey.
Eastern Chukchi beluga. Abundance estimate 13,305 from 2017.
Arctic ringed seal, listed as threatened. Abundance undetermined.

Up to six moorings and two drifting buoys pulse 30 seconds every four hours for a year, so gliders under the ice can fix a position by trilateration.

The machine half is exact to the second. The animal half is stale or blank.

Nine frames descend one column of water, from four mitigation zones at true metre scale down to a stock dial with no needle.

Year 10 is already inside Year 9's comment scope. How does the seal's blank survive nine years of one year permits?

#MarineMammalProtectionAct #ArcticResearch #AlaskaAI

deck_summary: Nine frames descend one column of water, from four mitigation zones at true metre scale down to a stock dial with no needle.

slides.headline: The permit can find the robot. It can't count the seal.

slides.kicker:
POSITION BY DISTANCE,
IN THE NOTICE'S WORDS
slides.headline: Sound is how the machine knows where it is.
slides.body: Above the ice, a glider gets its position from a satellite modem. Under the ice, that signal can't reach it. The notice says gliders then navigate by trilateration from moored acoustic sound sources, the geometry of intersecting circles.
labels:
GLIDERS TRANSIT TO DEPTHS OF
UP TO 1,000 m
slides.provenance: SATELLITE FIXES DO NOT REACH UNDER ICE. THIS PAGE'S GLOSS
slides.note: Kicker replaced twice. HOW A MACHINE UNDER ICE KNOWS WHERE IT IS repeated five of the headline's eight words directly above it. The first replacement, UNDER ICE, A POSITION IS THREE DISTANCES, was refused by aggregate_check and rightly: the notice's own parenthetical defines trilateration as determining location by measurement of distances using the geometry of circles, spheres or triangles, and it never says three, so the number was this page's inference printed as the record's. The shipped string carries the mechanism and no count.

slides.headline:
30 seconds,
every four hours,
all year.
slides.body: Up to six moorings are fixed acoustic navigation sources at 900 to 950 Hz. Each sends a 30 second pulse every four hours. Two buoys drift on that cycle. Levels this year stay under 185 dB re 1 uPa at 1 m.
labels:
NTE 185 dB
re 1 uPa at 1 m
slides.provenance: PULSE AND CEILING, THE NOTICE'S. PROPORTIONS, THE DRAWING'S

slides.headline:
About 639,237
square kilometres
of water.
slides.body: Its closest point to the Alaska coast is 204 kilometres, or 110 nautical miles. The work crosses the US exclusive economic zone, the high seas north of Alaska, and part of Canada's.
labels:
THREE JURISDICTIONS,
ONE OF THEM CANADA'S
slides.provenance: AREA IS THE NOTICE'S. THE MOTE COUNT IS THE DRAWING'S

slides.kicker:
THE MITIGATION ZONES,
DRAWN TO ONE SCALE
slides.headline:
Every zone here,
drawn at one
scale.
slides.body: Vessels hold 457 metres from observed cetaceans and 183 metres from other observed marine mammals. Deployment and recovery of a source carries a 55 metre zone. The estimated range to temporary hearing threshold shift is under 15 metres.
slides.lower_band_line: The 55 metre zone applies during deployment and recovery, not for the year the source then transmits.
labels:
LEVEL A HARASSMENT
NEITHER ANTICIPATED
NOR AUTHORIZED
slides.provenance: ALL FOUR RADII ARE THE NOTICE'S. THE SCALE IS THIS PAGE'S

slides.kicker:
WHAT RUNS AFTER
THE SHIP GOES HOME
slides.headline:
A 22 day cruise.
A full year of
transmission.
slides.body: The cruise is planned for 22 days from September 22nd, on a ship the notice calls ice strengthened rather than icebreaking. The sources keep transmitting until September 13th, 2027. Mitigation that needs an observer works only while one is aboard.
slides.provenance: CYCLE AND TERM, THE NOTICE'S. THE TALLY IS THE DRAWING'S

slides.headline:
The same page
gives the seal's
number as UND.
slides.body: Beaufort beluga, 39,258, from a 1992 survey. Eastern Chukchi beluga, 13,305, from 2017, at a coefficient of variation of 0.51. Arctic ringed seal, the one species here listed as threatened, undetermined.
slides.provenance: RING RADIUS IS A COEFFICIENT OF VARIATION, NOT A DISTANCE

slides.kicker:
THE NINTH YEAR,
ONE AT A TIME
slides.headline:
Position, fixed.
The rest is
undetermined.
slides.body: The authorization runs from September 14th and by statute can't run longer than a year. This is the ninth year of the project. It relies on a Biological Opinion issued on September 13th, 2022. Three private citizens wrote in.
labels:
THE RECORD'S DEEPEST
STATED DEPTH IS 2,000 m.
BELOW THAT, DRAWN
AND NOT MEASURED.
slides.provenance: SEABED DEPTH DOES NOT APPEAR IN THE NOTICE
slides.note: Kicker changed from NINE YEARS to THE NINTH YEAR after the aggregate gate. C06 says this authorization covers the ninth year of the project; it does not print the number nine, so NINE YEARS was an assertion the record does not carry in those words and aggregate_check was right to refuse it. The ordinal is what the notice says and it still satisfies the frame's own acceptance test, that the count refers to YEARS and never to a stack of documents.

slides.headline:
The robot's fix
or the seal's
number.
slides.body: Year 10 is already inside the comment scope of Year 9. Which of those two numbers should the next authorization improve?
slides.note: No provenance or source note appears on this frame, and none may. The dossier carries the owner change of 2026-09-11 as a hard layout rule for the close, and the copywriter supplied one anyway. The render is right and this entry was wrong.
